title: The Chicago-based Miss Broadway show and arranger Professor Randolph
summary: Only three musicians in the show band were from New Orleans; Professor Randolph wrote arrangements and specialty numbers.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, this other, this Broadway, were all the musicians from up north then in Chicago or some of them down here, from here too?
We only had, let's see, I remember, we only had three musicians in that band from here.
What's the name of the band? Just three. What's the name of the band? Just three from here.

That was myself, Lionel Furbaugh, played trumpet, and a tenor player you called Antwine. Yeah, I don't know. I might have heard of him on that. In fact, I haven't seen Antwine in a long time. When I see Lionel Furbaugh quite often. But that was the only three men in this Miss Broadway show from here at that time. All the rest of them was from Chicago.
How did they play? Did you notice any difference in their style? Did they play much jazz or mostly just other songs for the show?

Or how? Well, at that time, the most playing that we done in that band was the music we played for the show, for the performers. And well this professor, Professor Randolph, he had pretty good ideas about jazz then at that time, because he was writing some arrangements, that is, for the bands to do specialists. Had special spots along during the show that the band would do specialists. Well he had wrote some nice stuff for a band to do specialists.

Roofing Randolph, I forget his first name, had worked with Louis Armstrong later, and he wrote to old man Moe. He says, Randolph, I used to hear him in Chicago. He'd been with Armstrong for a while, sort of organized his band, played second trumpet with him. Well this Randolph was a violin player. Oh no, this was a trumpet player.

And that's all I knew then at that time was Professor Randolph. Well it might be a relative of his, that's what you're thinking of. Well he's from Chicago. But he had pretty good ideas, that is, of writing swing music at that time, because he used to write some nice stuff, that is, for overtures. And along by the middle way of the show we had certain numbers we would do, the band would do. Well he would write those himself. And they were somewhat on time, at that time.
